method: per model: read coefficient from read-only runs, then least squares for output and cache write with the read term removed; first call or first parallel batch of each run is the baseline reading; runs crossing 100% excluded. Overnight 2026-11-10 00:12–02:06 UTC added one 18-tick run per class for Opus and Sonnet.

fable-5-1.w_read_note: one tick on 2.38M read tokens (0.44/Mtok) set to 0: the back-test lands within ±1 point with 0 and runs 15–45% high with 0.44

haiku-5-5.w_read_note: one tick on 0.85M; treated as 0 like every other model

fable-5-2.w_read_note: fit says 2.7 on 3 ticks over 1.12M read, but 2 of the 3 ticks arrived on the first read call right after the 101k load and the next ten reads produced 1 tick on 1.02M: a one-call lag of the load cost, not a read cost. Set to 0 like every other model; upper bound ≈1/Mtok.

backtest.note: interactive-only intervals with a meter reading within 3 min of both ends; predicted from deduplicated transcripts with the table; Fable read weight 0

notes: Fable 5.2 (claude-fable-5-2) measured 2026-11-10 06:31–06:47 UTC; it draws on the same scoped weekly "Fable" bucket as 5.1 (bucket moved 44 → 51 during its runs).

Event lag: on Fable 5.2 a large cache write showed up in the NEXT call's rate_limit_event, not its own (write run: 68k at call 1 read 0.17, then 0.19 at call 2). With call 0 as baseline this leaks call 0's cost into the run and drops the last call's; for equal-sized calls they cancel, for a small call 0 the run reads a few % low. Within the quoted bars.
